technical-summary: A production start with the live policy on stopped itself 15 s after reaching running: the steady-state heat guard found 'the launch-bound proof beside the histogram does not match this launch and file' for all six of its re-reads (a fixed 100 ms window). The engine publishes the raw histogram and then its proof with two renames; a poll between them sees the new file beside the previous proof, and a loaded disk can stretch the gap past 100 ms. The re-read window is now time-bounded and derived from the manifest's declared histogram period (never below the old 100 ms), and a persistent mismatch names the fields that differ (launch nonce, file identity, size, modification time, or no readable proof) so a recurrence is diagnosable. The cause of the one observed failure is not proven (no trace of the transient survives); this removes the race as an explanation and records the evidence next time.
user-summary-candidate: A busy disk no longer makes a policy-on production start stop itself over a momentarily mismatched heat proof, and a real mismatch says what differs.
